regulations_applicable.title: Agency 30 - KANSAS DEPARTMENT FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court dismissed the appeal for lack of jurisdiction, holding that K.S.A. 38-2273(a) limits appealable CINC orders to the five listed categories and that post-termination permanency orders — including a finding that the agency failed to make reasonable efforts toward adoptive placement and the resulting change of custody to foster parents — are not appealable.
key_cases.relevance: Permanency-hearing requirements continue after termination until adoption or appointment of a permanent custodian, but decisions made at those hearings are unappealable under the Code.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Revised Code's appellate jurisdiction statute, K.S.A. 2012 Supp. 38-2273(a), limits what district court decisions may be appealed in a CINC proceeding

key_cases.holding: The court dismissed a grandmother's appeal for lack of jurisdiction, holding that K.S.A. 38-2273(a) permits appeal only of temporary custody, adjudication, disposition, unfitness, and termination orders, and that orders addressing a child's placement — as distinct from custody — are not reviewable.
key_cases.relevance: Interested parties who want to contest an older youth's continuing placement must find an appealable custody order, because placement rulings alone cannot be reviewed.
key_cases.quote: orders addressing the placement of a child are not dispositional orders, and K.S.A. 38-2273(a) does not vest appellate courts with jurisdiction to review such orders

key_cases.case_name: In re Guardianship & Conservatorship of B.H.
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the Court of Appeals and remanded, holding that the parental preference doctrine governs a parent's petition to terminate a voluntary guardianship absent unfitness or extraordinary circumstances, and that the district court's findings were too sparse to permit appellate review of whether extraordinary circumstances existed.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion warns against migrating a child's care out of the Code for Care of Children into the Probate Code, which matters for older youth whose permanency is handled by guardianship.
key_cases.quote: Because we determine that the district court findings were insufficient to allow proper appellate review, we remand the case to the district court for more complete and specific findings
